status_summary: A presidential memorandum of 2025-01-20 directed Commerce and USTR to review trade deficits, unfair foreign trade practices and existing trade agreements and report by 2025-04-01; it applies to all major partners and does not name the EU or UK. The US and UK announced the Economic Prosperity Deal general terms on 2025-05-08, and Executive Order 14309 (signed 2025-06-16) implemented auto, aerospace and steel and aluminum provisions. The US and EU issued a joint statement on a framework on 2025-08-21, which describes itself as a first step and uses non-binding language, and a Federal Register notice of 2025-09-25 implemented its tariff elements. The Supreme Court held on 2026-02-20 that the emergency-powers statute does not authorize tariffs; law-firm summaries report a 10 percent Section 122 surcharge from 2026-02-24, EU implementation of its side from 2026-07-01, and Section 301 tariffs from 2026-07-24 setting the EU at up to 10 percent combined and the UK at 10 percent. The approach is a government-wide, tariff-driven review followed by deals, not an EU-specific review.

timeline.event: The America First Trade Policy memorandum directed Commerce and USTR to report by 2025-04-01 on the causes of persistent trade deficits, on unfair trade practices by other countries, and on revisions to existing trade agreements needed for reciprocal concessions; it does not name the EU or UK.
The US and UK announced the general terms of the Economic Prosperity Deal, per USTR's listing.
Executive Order 14309 implemented the general terms of the US-UK Economic Prosperity Deal.
The US and EU issued a joint statement on a framework for an agreement on reciprocal, fair and balanced trade; the text calls itself a first step and does not say it is binding.

A Commerce and USTR Federal Register notice amended the tariff schedule to implement tariff-related elements of the US-EU framework, including 15 percent combined rates for EU autos and parts and MFN-only treatment for certain goods.
The Supreme Court held 6-3 in Learning Resources v. Trump that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act does not authorize tariffs.

timeline.event: A law-firm tracker reported that the EU trade deal took effect after the Council of the EU adopted two regulations on 2026-06-25, with most EU products facing a 15 percent US rate.

The Section 122 surcharge expired as new Section 301 tariffs took effect, with the EU at a combined rate of up to 10 percent net of MFN and the UK at a flat 10 percent stacking on MFN, per a law-firm summary.

title: Review US-EU trade for fairness and reciprocity; develop trade with the post-Brexit UK
uncertainties: The 2026-07-01 EU entry-into-force date, the Section 122 and Section 301 details and the UK digital services tax proposal rest on law-firm trackers, not on primary EU or US documents. The April 2025 reports produced under the trade memorandum were not read, so how far they addressed EU arrangements specifically is unknown. The date of the UK White House fact sheet is approximate. Inference: match was changed to partial because the Mandate asks for a fairness and reciprocity review and closer UK trade, which the memorandum's review and the resulting deals address in substance, though by tariff leverage and not by an EU-specific review.
